chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Abī Ayyūb, who said:
Muḥammad ibn Muslim asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, while I was listening, about the traveler: if he resolves within himself to stay for ten days, he said: then let him complete the salat (prayer).
But if he does not know how long he will stay, whether a day or more, then let him count thirty days, and then let him complete; even if he has stayed one day or one salat (prayer).
Then Muḥammad ibn Muslim said to him: It has reached me that you said five. He said: I did say that. Abū Ayyūb said: Then I said, May I be made your ransom, can it be less than five? He said: No.

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan, may Allah have mercy on him, said: What this report contains of the instruction to complete for one who intends to stay five days admits of two possibilities: one of them is that it is to be understood as recommendation, and the second is that it is specific to one who is in Makkah or al-Madīnah; and that which indicates this is:

key_terms.إِقَامَةِ: intending to remain in a place for a specified duration
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation rather than obligation in legal interpretation
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرِ: the traveler who is subject to special rulings regarding salat (prayer)
key_terms.ثَلَاثِينَ يَوْمًا: the thirty-day period counted when the duration of stay is uncertain
key_terms.خَمْسَةَ أَيَّامٍ: the five-day period mentioned in the report and discussed by the compiler
key_terms.عَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ: the ten-day period that establishes completion of salat (prayer)
key_terms.فَلْيُتِمَّ: let him perform the salat (prayer) in full rather than shortened form

ai.seo_question: When must a traveler complete the salat (prayer) if he does not know how long he will stay?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a traveler entering a town without certainty about the duration of stay and when he must perform the salat (prayer) in full. It also records a transmitted scholarly clarification by Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan concerning the report about five days, indicating possible reconciliation through recommendation or restricting it to Makkah or al-Madīnah.
